inputs.sbc_source: 10-K/Annual FY2025 note 8 Expenses by Nature (share based payments $47k) and cash-flow-statement addback; SBC-zero market -- immaterial, held at 0% in projections per section 7(e)
inputs.share_count_basis: fully diluted weighted-average shares per FY2025 10-K/Annual Report note (127,614,019), unchanged since FY2023; dilutive LTI awards are currently anti-dilutive given losses and are excluded
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-08-20T03:42:36Z regular NZX session (Yahoo Finance regularMarketTime; not after-hours)
inputs.balance_sheet_date: 2025-12-31 (H1-2026 interim report, most recent available; net debt/cash anchors refreshed to this date rather than the 30-Jun-2025 annual)
notes: MODEL CHOICE: Owner-FCF DCF (operating company: NZ domestic freight/logistics), routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md. Not a bank/REIT/LIC/holdco, so the standard owner-FCF engine applies with section 7 non-US/cyclical adaptations (currency, leases, SBC-zero market).

LEASE TREATMENT: Section 7(b) treatment (B) -- 'leases as operating cost'. Lease principal repayments (IFRS 16, sit in financing per the cash flow statement) are DEDUCTED from owner FCF (~10.2-11.0% of revenue historically) as a capex-like fleet-renewal cost, consistent with the company operating a mostly-leased truck fleet with near-zero PPE capex (FY2025 PPE purchases were only $0.186m). Lease liabilities ($146.98m at H1-2026: $28.14m current + $118.83m non-current) are EXCLUDED from net_debt/total_debt, which is bank borrowings only ($21.418m, all current at H1-2026 -- see going-concern note). This is internally consistent: nothing is charged twice.

REPORTED FCF IS FLATTERED: MOV.NZ's reported/CSV FreeCashFlow line (OCF less minimal capex) looks strongly positive in FY2024-25 (+$16.8m, +$25.1m) purely because IFRS 16 lease principal sits in the financing section, not operating. Once lease principal is deducted, TRUE owner FCF was NEGATIVE every year FY2023-FY2025 (-$8.0m, -$12.7m, -$5.8m) and only turned marginally positive in H1-2026 (+$1.42m, vs -$6.63m in H1-2025). The going-concern note itself flags 'the impact of the current lease liability... on the working capital deficit' -- this is not a modelling artefact, it is the company's own disclosed reading of its cash position.

last_fcf is TTM owner FCF reconstructed as FY2025 + H1-2026 - H1-2025 = -5.824 + 1.422 - (-6.626) = $2.224m, the freshest trailing owner-FCF anchor available and consistent with the H1-2026 balance-sheet date used for net debt.
SBC is genuinely immaterial ($47k FY2025, $0 FY2024) -- SBC-zero market per section 7(e). House and street bases coincide; band_position set to null rather than a degenerate 0%.

GOING CONCERN: FY2025 and H1-2026 both concluded NO material uncertainty (post amended ANZ covenants + new BNZ facility effective Nov-2026), but H1-2026 working-capital deficit widened to $39.2m (from $27.9m at FY2025) with $21.4m of ANZ borrowings classified entirely current (due for refinancing within 12 months) and total equity of only $10.58m against $209.1m total liabilities. This is a real, live solvency risk, not a resolved historical one -- it is charged in the bear-case probability weight (30%) and the bear scenario's negative equity outcome, per section 7(f) 'charge risk once' (a single 16.5% WACC is used across all three scenarios; risk is NOT additionally stacked into the discount rate).

HISTORICAL CAGRs NOT USED AS FORWARD DRIVERS: revenue 3yr/5yr CAGR are both negative (shrinking business, FY2022 $360m peak -> FY2025 $286m) and equity CAGR is deeply negative and distorted by a FY2022 capital raise followed by accumulated losses -- neither is a sensible proxy for a turnaround inflecting off a trough. Forward growth/margin paths are instead built bottom-up from FY2026 guidance (positive NEBT achieved, positive FCF restored per the 24-Jul-2026 trading update) and the H1-2026 print, per section 2's component-build methodology.

P/Sales of ~0.09x and EV/EBITDA of ~4.4x (even grossing ALL lease liabilities into EV) confirm the stock trades at a deep going-concern/solvency discount to its underlying revenue and EBITDA base -- the large base-case upside is a legitimate reading of that discount, not a modelling error; it is why the bear weight is held at 30% rather than the house default 15%.

TAX TREATMENT: NOPAT = pretax income x (1 - cash tax rate), applied symmetrically even in years with negative pretax income (i.e. a tax benefit accrues on losses as the ramping cash tax rate is applied) -- this is the Excel workbook's authoritative formula (DCF_Bear row 19 = row17*(1-row18)) and the JSON was reconciled to match it exactly. Only the bear case is affected (5 of 10 years have negative pretax income); base and bull have at most one negative-pretax year at a 0% tax rate, so the two treatments coincide there. Workbook and JSON now agree on base/bull/bear IV, entry price and weighted IV to the cent.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: not historical CAGR -- FY2026(Y1) guided revenue decline of ~-1.0%, the first year of the bottom-up base-case build (see inputs.notes); all historical revenue/equity/EPS/FCF CAGRs are negative and describe a business in structural decline through the distress period, not a usable forward proxy for a turnaround inflecting off FY2025-26 trough
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR (-46.1%) and 5yr CAGR (-20.9%) diverge massively from revenue CAGR (-7.4%/-3.0%) -- equity collapse is driven by accumulated losses ($76.8m) against a FY2022 capital-raise-inflated starting equity base ($72.99m), not by the underlying revenue trend. Equity CAGR is NOT used as the growth-rate source for this reason.
historical_growth.notes: SBC-adjusted FCF CAGR is not meaningful either: owner FCF (post lease-principal deduction) was negative in FY2023, FY2024 AND FY2025, so no CAGR can be computed on a negative-to-negative (or negative-to-less-negative) series. Reported FCF, by contrast, looks like it grew (+19.3m FY23 -> +25.1m FY25) -- entirely a lease-financing-placement artefact, not real cash generation; see inputs.notes for the reported-vs-owner reconciliation.

wacc_rationale: Single WACC of 16.5% used across ALL THREE scenarios (bear/base/bull), per section 7(f) 'charge risk once': cyclicality, customer concentration and going-concern/refinancing risk are priced into the SCENARIO FLOWS and PROBABILITY WEIGHTS (30% bear), not stacked again as a per-scenario WACC premium. Build: NZ 10-year government bond ~4.5% risk-free + NZ equity risk premium ~6.5% + a substantial company-specific premium (~5.5pp) for micro-cap illiquidity (thin free float, ~NZD 26m market cap), a going-concern history resolved only via two rounds of ANZ covenant renegotiation in the past 18 months, and 100% of current bank debt due for refinancing within 12 months. This sits well above the ~9% house reference for a stable JPY keiretsu industrial and the ~10.5% USD tech default -- appropriately so, given MOV.NZ actually disclosed material going-concern uncertainty as recently as its FY2024 annual report.
valuation_philosophy: MOV.NZ is a distressed NZ freight/logistics turnaround roughly 18 months into a two-year 'Accelerate' cost-out programme, trading at ~0.09x P/Sales and ~NZD 26m market cap against NZD 286m of FY2025 revenue. The central finding of this model is that MOST of the reported FY2024-25 'FCF recovery' narrative is an IFRS-16 accounting artefact: lease principal on the company's largely-leased truck fleet sits in the financing section of the cash flow statement, flattering reported OCF/FCF, while true owner FCF (after deducting that principal as the real cost of running the fleet) was negative every year from FY2023 through FY2025 and only turned marginally positive in H1-2026 (+$1.42m). The valuation is built bottom-up from FY2026 guidance (positive NEBT achieved, FCF 'restored to positive' per the 24-Jul-2026 trading update) rather than from historical CAGRs, which are uniformly negative and describe the collapse, not the turnaround. A single 16.5% WACC is used across all scenarios so that cyclicality, customer concentration and refinancing risk are priced once, in the scenario flows and a heavier-than-default 30% bear weight, not doubled into the discount rate. The bear case is explicitly a going-concern-relapse scenario with negative implied equity value -- a legitimate outcome given equity of only NZD 10.6m against NZD 209m of liabilities and a working-capital deficit that WIDENED between FY2025 ($27.9m) and H1-2026 ($39.2m). The resulting wide spread between bear (-$0.09) and bull ($1.17) is the honest picture of a name where solvency, not multiple, is the swing factor.

base.narrative: Base case: the Accelerate programme's ~$27m annualised cost-out holds, three of four divisions (Freight & Fuel, Specialist, International) stay profitable and Warehousing gradually stabilises rather than turns around, and NZ consumer demand recovers only slowly. Revenue troughs in FY2026 (guided as roughly flat/-1% given the weak H1 print) before a modest low-single-digit recovery as the economy improves and the Cook Strait ferry rail-capacity tailwind starts to help South Island volumes from FY2027-28. EBITDA margin recovers from FY2025's 14.7% toward a MATURE 16.0% -- below the FY2021 COVID-freight-boom peak of 17.4%, reflecting a permanently more competitive Warehousing market and MOV's sub-scale position versus Mainfreight/Freightways. Cash tax is sheltered by accumulated losses through Y1-Y2, ramping to the NZ 28% statutory rate by Y8. Two years of residual Accelerate restructuring cash costs ($2.0m Y1, $0.8m Y2) taper to zero.

bull.narrative: Bull case: New Horizons roadmap delivers in full -- Warehousing reset succeeds (new customer wins convert, site consolidation lifts margin), the Oceans trans-Tasman shipping pilot scales into a genuine third profit engine, the Specialist division's renewable-energy/roading pipeline ramps from FY2027 as guided, and the Cook Strait rail-ferry-retirement tailwind materially redirects South Island freight to MOV's network. NZ economic recovery is faster and broader than base case. Revenue resumes mid-single-digit growth by Y3-Y5 and EBITDA margin recovers to 19% -- above the FY2021 COVID peak, reflecting a genuinely leaner permanent cost base layered onto a real volume recovery, not just cyclical operating leverage.

bear.narrative: Bear case: the going-concern relapse scenario. NZ recession persists or deepens, Warehousing's structural decline continues with no turnaround, 'irrational' competitor pricing spreads into Freight & Fuel, and the single >10%-of-revenue customer relationship comes under renegotiation pressure. Revenue keeps shrinking through Y1-Y4 before stabilising at a permanently smaller base (~$258m, below even FY2025). EBITDA margin falls back toward FY2024's 9.4% trough before a slow partial recovery to only 13% -- the cost-out gains are eroded by wage/competitive pressure faster than volume returns. Interest costs rise as covenant renegotiation becomes costlier (banks price the risk MOV itself flagged in its own going-concern notes), and a heavier, longer restructuring cash tail ($3.0m/$2.0m/$1.0m/$0.5m across Y1-Y4) reflects a further cost-out round. This is the scenario the FY2024 going-concern qualification was warning about, recurring.

bear.note: Bear case implies NEGATIVE equity value (equity -$8.56m from EV of only $4.72m against $13.28m net debt) -- a legitimate going-concern-relapse outcome, not a floor-at-zero artefact (terminal-year owner FCF is positive at $6.84m so the TV floor is not triggered; the negative result comes from four years of cash-burning interim flows during the relapse, only turning FCF-positive in Y5). Flagged per section 4: 'a bear case sitting on the floor is telling you the business does not survive that path' -- here the path is survivable in the model but destroys essentially all equity value along the way. NOPAT uses a symmetric tax treatment (NOPAT = pretax x (1-tax_rate), applied even when pretax is negative, i.e. a tax benefit accrues on losses in Y5-Y10 as the cash tax rate ramps up from the accumulated-loss shelter) -- this is the Excel workbook's formula and is authoritative; it differs slightly from a max(0,pretax) floored tax-base treatment.

base.entry_price_correction_note: Terminal value rebuilt at the hurdle rate 2026-09-01: min(Gordon@hurdle, cap x FCF_N). The superseded value held the WACC-built terminal value and varied only the discounting.

bull.entry_price_correction_note: Terminal value rebuilt at the hurdle rate 2026-09-01: min(Gordon@hurdle, cap x FCF_N). The superseded value held the WACC-built terminal value and varied only the discounting.

entry_price.note: Entry price (15% hurdle) sits slightly ABOVE the WACC-discounted intrinsic value in base/bull because the house WACC (16.5%) exceeds the 15% hurdle for this name -- the opposite of the usual pattern in this folder, where WACC is typically below 15%. That inversion is a direct, correctly-signed consequence of pricing MOV.NZ's real going-concern/refinancing risk into a higher-than-usual discount rate; it is not a formula error.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's required return (min(Gordon@r, cap x FCF_N)), so the flows and the exit are charged the same rate. Corrected 2026-09-01.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear weight raised to 30% (house default 15%) per section 3's explicit trigger for going-concern risk and covenant pressure: MOV.NZ carried a DISCLOSED material going-concern uncertainty as recently as its FY2024 annual report, and while both FY2025 and H1-2026 concluded no material uncertainty remains, the underlying working-capital deficit WIDENED ($27.9m -> $39.2m) over that same window and 100% of current bank borrowings are due for refinancing within 12 months. Bull weight trimmed to 25% (below the house 35% default) because the bull case requires several largely-independent things to go right simultaneously (Warehousing turnaround, Oceans shipping scaling, Specialist pipeline ramp, AND a broader NZ economic recovery) rather than one dominant lever. Base carries the remaining 45%.

sanity_check.basis_note: Multiples computed on GAAP figures (SBC is nil for MOV.NZ, so SBC-adjusted equals unadjusted). P/E unavailable: net income negative FY2022-FY2025 and marginal earlier. FY-end = June-30 closes matched to each FY row. FY2018/FY2019 EV/EBITDA are pre-IFRS16 and not comparable to FY2020+; the maxima below use the post-IFRS16 window FY2020-FY2025.
sanity_check.diagnosis: No trip. Implied EV/EBITDA 2.19x is within the FY2020-FY2025 historical range (0.97-2.57x) and implied P/Sales 0.26x is mid-range (0.08-0.43x). Implied P/B 6.61x is elevated but below the 1.5x-of-10yr-max threshold (1.5 x 4.95 = 7.43); book equity has been impaired down to NZ$11.4m so P/B mechanically inflates and is the weakest anchor for this turnaround. Base upside is 188% but the NZ$0.205 price sits near the 10-year low (range ~0.175-2.03), so the upside-with-elevated-price trip does not apply.
